findings.description: The gate-evidence workflow writes the shared TinySOL cache (same key and path as ci.yml) without TinySOL_metadata.csv, which only ci.yml downloads; every later ci.yml reference run on impl-<run_id> restores it, passes the 689-file count and the WAV-only hash list, and fails T-200 at tinysol_root() ('TinySOL_metadata.csv is missing').
findings.lens: dependency and supply-chain drift; operational realities
findings.conditions: actions/cache saves only on job success; no ci.yml reference job can succeed before the accordion is implemented and calibrated, while the G-P1 gate-evidence job at S-210 succeeds, so it is expected to write the key first; the entry is used on every push and never evicted
findings.root_cause: two workflows share one cache key but have different download steps; the R-053 hash list covers only the WAV files and no post-cache check covers the metadata file
findings.traces_to: plan/ci/gate-evidence.yml 'Download TinySOL if not cached'; plan/ci/ci.yml reference job; R-053; S-210, S-330 (DR-13), S-340 action 2, S-LISTEN action 4
findings.failure_path: S-210 pushes [gate-evidence G-P1 harmonica seed=1] -> cache miss -> archive extracted without metadata -> job succeeds -> cache saved -> every later ci.yml reference run hits it -> T-200 fixture fails -> S-330 cannot finish where Zenodo is unreachable locally (DR-13 needs the CI job green); every listening gate record names a red reference job; the fix needs a workflow edit or a cache deletion that the plan does not provide for; the pull request is green only because pr-** has its own cache scope, which hides the defect
findings.mitigation: Make the TinySOL download step identical in both workflows (gate-evidence.yml also downloads and md5-checks TinySOL_metadata.csv), and add to both workflows a step after the cache that requires TinySOL_metadata.csv with md5 a86c9bb115f69e61f2f25872e397fc4a
findings.mitigation_adds: the cache content is the same whichever workflow writes it, and a hit without the metadata fails loudly at the cache step, not inside T-200

findings.description: A change to shared DSP code (reed.cpp and the reed tables for harmonica, accordion and melodion; pluck.cpp for mandolin and bouzouki) made after a listening gate has closed alters that instrument's sound, and nothing re-opens the gate or ties a gate record to the commit it judged; the pull request presents audio the owner never heard as having passed.
findings.lens: integration; technical correctness; past lessons; integrity
findings.conditions: an iterate response at a later gate of the same family (the iterate procedure requires general mechanisms, so changes land in shared code), or any G-L1 question-4, S-REVIEW-DELTA or S-INTEGRATE fix to shared DSP; gates may be open together and close in any order
findings.root_cause: gate sign-off is per gate and per round, but code is shared across gates; DR-12 re-runs only the frozen suite and S-300's Done when; lessons L-20261009T193614Z and L-20261009T192606Z are not applied
findings.traces_to: S-LISTEN, DR-12, HANDOFF section 9 (iterate step 5), S-REVIEW-DELTA, S-INTEGRATE, GATES G-L1 to G-L5; lessons L-20261009T193614Z, L-20261009T192606Z
findings.failure_path: G-L1 harmonica answered proceed at commit X -> G-L3 iterate changes the attack in core/src/reed.cpp -> frozen suite passes -> G-L1 stays closed -> S-REVIEW-DELTA and S-INTEGRATE Done when pass -> the pull request links GATE-G-L1.md as passed for a harmonica the owner never heard; for harmonica and melodion (no pairs) the gate is the only realism check
findings.mitigation: Each gate record names the commit of the audio it judged; before S-REVIEW-DELTA completes, run git diff --quiet <gate commit> HEAD -- core/ presets/ tools/folk-render/ for every closed gate; if it is non-empty for files the instrument uses, open a confirmation round of that gate (new demos, new seed, same questions, not counted against the round limit)
findings.mitigation_adds: approved means approved as shipped; applies the provenance lessons; a confirmation round costs one listening session only when shared code actually changed

findings.description: check_tsan_supp.py accepts any line of the form race:juce::Name(::Name)*, including class-level or short prefixes (race:juce::A, race:juce::AudioBuffer, race:juce::MidiBuffer). ThreadSanitizer suppressions are unanchored substring templates matched against every frame's demangled function name, which includes parameter types, so such a line also matches the wrapper's own frames, e.g. FolkProcessor::processBlock(juce::AudioBuffer<float>&, juce::MidiBuffer&), and suppresses every wrapper race in T-304.
findings.lens: technical correctness (real-time safety); security of the verification
findings.conditions: host-tsan reports a JUCE-internal race that ENVIRONMENT section 5 lets the implementer suppress, the implementer writes a class-level or prefix pattern (which T-092 accepts), and the wrapper has a real race
findings.root_cause: the checker validates syntax but not the matching semantics; the 'folk' ban is useless because the match comes from JUCE types in wrapper signatures; the canary's frames contain no JUCE type, so it cannot detect over-suppression
findings.traces_to: tests/ci/check_tsan_supp.py (frozen), T-092, tests/ci/tsan_canary.cpp, ci.yml host-tsan, ENVIRONMENT section 5, D-094, R-021, R-051
findings.failure_path: S-003/S-320 host-tsan red on a JUCE-internal report -> tsan.supp gains race:juce::AudioBuffer with a DEVIATIONS entry -> T-092 checker passes -> the suppression also matches the audio-side processBlock frame of any wrapper race -> host-tsan green -> a wrapper data race ships
findings.mitigation: Amend check_tsan_supp.py and T-092 (planner amendment before implementation) to require race:^juce::<Class>::<function> (leading ^ mandatory, at least two name components) and to reject unanchored lines
findings.mitigation_adds: a suppression can match only frames whose function name begins with juce::, so no folk:: frame can ever be suppressed whatever its parameter types

findings.description: Code changed after S-REVIEW-DELTA is not reviewed: S-INTEGRATE depends on S-REVIEW-DELTA, but its own actions (merge of a moved main, red-check fixes 'on impl-<run_id>' under On failure, G-004 fix directions) never send the implementer back to it; the repeat rule is stated only inside S-REVIEW-DELTA.
findings.conditions: a red check on the pull request fixed in code, or origin/main moved
findings.root_cause: the repeat condition sits in the earlier step and covers only a merge
findings.traces_to: S-REVIEW-DELTA, S-INTEGRATE actions 1 to 4 and On failure, R-055
findings.failure_path: S-INTEGRATE On failure -> code fix on impl -> pr branch recreated -> checks green -> the pull request links DELTA_REVIEW.md, whose range ends before the fix
findings.mitigation: S-INTEGRATE action 4: if the head differs from the end of the range in reviews/DELTA_REVIEW.md, repeat S-REVIEW-DELTA for the difference before opening or refreshing the pull request
findings.mitigation_adds: every delivered line is inside a reviewed range

findings.description: The two control pairs are built from the first two references by id, which are also two of the 12 real pairs; prepare() is deterministic, so each control's reference clip is byte-identical (same digest in SHA256SUMS or PAIRS-SHA256SUMS) to the reference side of a real pair, which gives away two real answers.
findings.conditions: the listener recognises a repeated one-second clip (or reads the digests)
findings.root_cause: the controls draw on the scored references and the same window
findings.failure_path: S-340 control-1 = accordion-001 vs sine -> the same clip is the reference side of the accordion-001 real pair -> two answers known -> the score is inflated towards more than 8 -> spurious iterate rounds (which feed F-2)
findings.mitigation: Build the controls from the middle window of the reference, or from two references not used in the real pairs
findings.mitigation_adds: controls stay obvious without revealing any real pair

findings.description: The A/B key and control positions depend only on the seed and the stem names, both public; under seed 411 (G-L4 round 1 attempt 1) the key is AABBAAAABAAAAB, with 10 'A' and both controls 'A', so fourteen 'A' answers are valid (not side-biased against the key) and score 8 of 12, which passes.
findings.conditions: the melodion has 12 or more indexed references (C-051 found none), attempt 0 of round 1 was void, and the listener answers uniformly
findings.root_cause: the side-bias rule exempts a uniform answer when the key has 10 or more of that letter; the seeds are fixed in the plan
findings.traces_to: D-053 seeds and void rule, S-340 score_gate.py, R-034, R-056
findings.failure_path: simulation of make_blind_pairs with seed 411 and the melodion stems -> all-A answer -> controls correct, 8/12 -> verdict valid, pass condition met
findings.mitigation: Treat 10 or more of one letter as void unless every answer equals the key, or draw each seed at the gate from a secret source and record it after scoring
findings.mitigation_adds: no planned seed lets a non-listening answer pass

findings.description: gen_presets.py --check, now run in the CI core job (R-057), compares the committed header with regenerated firwin half-band coefficients; NumPy's sin and cos take CPU-dependent SIMD paths, so full-precision text can differ in the last place between the implementer's sandbox and a hosted runner, or between runner CPU models.
findings.conditions: the generator prints shortest-round-trip or 17-digit values and the sandbox and runner CPUs take different SIMD paths
findings.root_cause: an exact-text staleness check over floating-point values computed at run time
findings.traces_to: S-100 action 2, ci.yml core 'Generated tables match the preset files', R-057, D-086 (runner CPU variance)
findings.failure_path: S-320 core job on ubuntu-24.04 fails at gen_presets --check with no preset change, or flakes between runs; the implementer must guess between a stale header and noise
findings.mitigation: S-100: the generator writes coefficients rounded to 12 significant digits (or --check compares values numerically within 1e-12)
findings.mitigation_adds: the check fails only for real staleness

findings.description: The sine controls (R-052's fix) are caught by anyone who plays the files, so they no longer detect a casual listener who spots the sines and guesses the other 12 pairs; such a listener passes with probability 0.93 (R-022's original failure).
findings.conditions: the owner listens casually (laptop speakers, skimming)
findings.root_cause: a control that cannot fail an attentive listener also cannot detect an inattentive one
findings.traces_to: D-053, GATES G-L question 1, R-022, R-052
findings.failure_path: listener answers both sine controls correctly and the rest at random -> valid round, 6 of 12 expected -> pass
findings.mitigation: State in question 1 that each pair must be played through on headphones and that the score is necessary, not sufficient (already in GATES); no further control
findings.mitigation_adds: proportionate: keeps the record honest about what a pass shows

findings.description: fetch_references.py downloads every indexed archive whole into $RUNNER_TEMP on every CI run (only TinySOL is cached), with no size bound; a note found inside a multi-GB Zenodo dataset makes every reference job on main slow or out of disk.
findings.conditions: S-REF indexes a note inside a large archive (C-051 found none for most instruments)
findings.root_cause: the archive cache is per job in CI; S-REF has no size criterion
findings.traces_to: S-REF actions 3 and 5, D-052, ci.yml reference, gate-evidence fetch, R-028
findings.failure_path: S-REF indexes zenodo-<record> row -> each push downloads the archive -> runner disk (about 14 GB) or the time limit exceeded -> reference and all-green red with no code change
findings.mitigation: S-REF records archive sizes in archives.csv and refuses archives above 2 GB, or caches redistributable archives like TinySOL

findings.description: S-LISTEN's Done when accepts proceed-without-pairs in its first clause but its second clause requires, for every gate with pairs, a passing score or proceed-with-rescope; GATES and D-053 call proceed-without-pairs a rescope, so the intent is recoverable.
findings.conditions: two void attempts in one round and the owner answers proceed-without-pairs
findings.traces_to: S-LISTEN Done when, GATES G-L branches, D-053

findings.description: Restatements: C-012/013/014/017/039 tables (R-001); string decay (R-004); runner retirement (R-006); T-201 statistic in public logs (R-016); fork pull requests and private references (R-023); main red without code change (R-028); keys computable from public seeds (R-034); no redistributable notes for three instruments (R-037); setCurrentProgram constrained by prose only, T-304 never calls it (R-066).

C-027 air-damping term may be a factor of 2 too large: from Valette's resistance R = 2 pi eta_a + 2 pi d sqrt(pi eta_a rho_a f) one obtains eta_air = (rho_a/rho)(2 sqrt(2) M + 1)/(2 M^2) with the same M; strings.h, ka.py, pluck_ref.py and T-005 encode the claim without the 2; DR-07 cannot calibrate the air term.
findings.conditions: not established: the source could not be read

findings.description: host-tsan's canary proves ThreadSanitizer works on the runner but not that the build-tsan host programs are instrumented; a CMakeLists.txt that overwrites CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS would make T-304 pass uninstrumented.
findings.conditions: no concrete reason found for the implementer to overwrite the flags
findings.root_cause: positive control at tool level only

summary: Round 3: 13 entries. Open new or residual findings: 10. High: 3. F-1 (new, expected): gate-evidence poisons the shared TinySOL cache without the metadata file. F-2 (new, plausible): shared DSP changes after a gate closes ship audio nobody heard. F-3 (residual R-051, remote): unanchored suppression patterns match wrapper frames through JUCE parameter types. Medium: 6 (F-4 residual R-055, F-5, F-6, F-7, F-8 residual R-052, F-9). Low: 1 (F-10). No Critical. Restated: F-11. Speculative: F-12, F-13. Round-2 mitigations judged effective: the strengthened T-302 program case; the TinySOL hash list (WAVs only, see F-1); the TSan canary as a tool-level control; per-gate seeds (distinct keys, see F-6); repeat and proceed-without-pairs as allowed responses (see F-10). Present but incomplete: gen_presets --check in CI (F-7), S-REVIEW-DELTA (F-2, F-4).
